# Done plans

Finished plans, newest first, moved here by tumwater from PLANS.md's `## Done`. This file
only grows: search it with grep, or read one entry by its line range. Never read it whole.

## Done

### Platinum GTK 3 overlay scrollbar thumbs: declare a reference-derived minimum (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role; independent of the GTK 4 overlay breadth plan) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** Give GTK 3 overlay thumbs an explicit minimum when the theme disables their steppers. The GTK 3 sheet currently gives `scrollbar slider` borders and paint but no minimum dimensions; the finished GTK 4 breadth work does not cover this sheet. This is a declaration guarantee, not a claim about current rendered allocation.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, add `scrollbar.overlay-indicator slider { min-width: 12px; min-height: 12px; }`. Add a dated adaptation comment: the reference set has no GTK overlay scrollbar; reuse the ordinary 16px reference band minus the scrollbar's and slider's two 1px borders, as in GTK 4. Keep ordinary GTK 3 sizing and the overlay stepper policy intact. In `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, add `TestGtkTheme.test_overlay_scrollbar_thumb_minimum` using `assert_rule` for the new selector. Add `TestScrollbarStepperReference.test_overlay_thumb_minimum_matches_reference`: sample the black boundaries at x=200, y=462 and y=477 and the intervening `TROUGH` pixels from `setup_emaculation.png`; derive `band = bottom - top + 1`, parse the sheet with the existing guarded `gtk_css.read_theme_text` and `parse_css`, assert both scrollbar and slider borders are `1px solid {BLACK}`, and compare both new minima with `f"{band - 4}px"`. Under `## gtk` in `docs/invariants.md`, record this minimum-size guarantee and both tests; identify the missing GTK overlay reference surface and the existing GTK 4 reference-band calculation as the adaptation source.

**Acceptance criteria.** The overlay selector explicitly declares both 12px minima; deleting either declaration or changing its value fails the declaration and reference-derived checks. The reference test re-derives the band from lossless pixels rather than asserting a standalone size constant. Existing ordinary scrollbar and stepper tests pass. Limit implementation to these three files; introduce no visibility policy or rendered-geometry claim. `make check` passes.

### Platinum GTK 4 overlay scrollbar troughs: suppress inherited margins (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role; independent of the queued overlay thumb minimum breadth plan) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** Through the supported `make apply-gtk` user stylesheet import, remove toolkit spacing around overlay troughs in hovering and non-hovering states. The completed ordinary trough margin reset excludes overlays; the queued thumb breadth plan explicitly leaves spacing separate.

**Approach and files.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, add a grouped rule for `scrollbar.overlay-indicator.horizontal.hovering > range > trough`, `scrollbar.overlay-indicator.horizontal:not(.hovering) > range > trough`, and the corresponding two vertical selectors, declaring only `margin: 0`. These selectors override the stock base, orientation and non-hovering overlay margins. Add a dated adaptation comment: no reference shows GTK overlay trough spacing; reuse the ordinary trough's zero-margin policy. In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, add `TestGtk4Theme.test_scrollbar_overlay_trough_margins` using `assert_rule` to require zero margins on those four selectors. Under `## gtk` in `docs/invariants.md`, record this declaration guarantee, test and provenance: `/org/gnome/Adwaita/styles/base.css` in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libadwaita-1.so.0`, inspected 2026-10-29, supplies base trough margins of 9px, horizontal top/bottom and vertical left/right margins of 8px, and non-hovering overlay transverse margins of 4px. Keep library provenance outside CSS for `test_stands_alone`.

**Acceptance criteria.** Each orientation/state selector explicitly declares `margin: 0`; removing one or restoring a nonzero margin fails the new test. Existing ordinary margin, thumb paint and breadth tests pass. The invariant names the missing reference surface and the existing ordinary reset as the adaptation source; zero is a platform adaptation, not a sampled metric, and declaration checks do not prove rendered spacing or breadth. Limit implementation to these three files and trough margins; preserve overlay visibility policy and thumb dimensions. This plan can merge independently of the queued overlay thumb minimum breadth plan. `make check` passes.

### Separate Firefox profile transaction rollback from the installer (planned 2026-10-29 by the organize role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** Make the boundary between Firefox profile transaction mechanics and install/remove policy explicit. `tools/install_firefox.py` is the largest production Python module (347 lines); it currently combines CLI/profile-lock orchestration, install/remove decisions, and rollback behavior for partially published profile files. In particular, `_restore_file`, `_restore_user_js` and the rollback handler inside `_apply` manage recovery state while `firefox_user_files.py` owns the underlying reads and writes.

**Target structure.** Add `tools/firefox_transaction.py` to own rollback state and handlers: move `_restore_file` and `_restore_user_js` there, and expose one transaction operation that receives the ordered sheet destinations with their prior contents, the `user.js` path/prior/published contents, and the write operation. It publishes the two sheets followed by `user.js`, and on a write exception or interrupt restores published state and combines restoration diagnostics using the existing `ConfigError`. Keep source loading, destination validation, refusal of foreign sheets, profile locking, install/remove policy, and CLI handling in `install_firefox.py`. Keep path resolution and file reads/writes in their existing profile/file modules. Update installer imports and focused transaction tests (currently in `tests/test_install_firefox.py`) to exercise the extracted API; do not change install or rollback behavior.

**Acceptance criteria.** The new module contains the rollback bookkeeping and recovery handler; `install_firefox.py` delegates publication and recovery while retaining validation and policy. Existing failure and interrupt cases continue to verify restoration of old files, removal of newly created files, and combined diagnostics. No stale references to moved helpers remain in source, tests or documentation, and `make check` passes.

### Firefox Platinum content: paint about:telemetry's data payloads — the sections' tables, the histogram boxes and their bars and the copy and JSON-viewer buttons — with the landed table and push-button recipes (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; part 1/2, the about:telemetry furniture plan, is landed in PLANS-DONE.md, so its body, register and test class exist to extend; independent of the queued GTK places-sidebar plan — that one touches the GTK sheets and their suites, this one `theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userContent.css`, `tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py` and `docs/invariants.md`) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed `about:telemetry` body paints only the page's furniture — the sidebar rows, the `#search` field, the `#stores` menu and the `#ping-picker` panel — so the sections' data payloads still paint stock: the JS-built tables keep Firefox's grey `--border-color` cell rules, the `.histogram` boxes keep the stock rounded grey-bordered box, each bar's `.bar-inner` keeps Firefox's accent-blue fill with its rounded rgba border, and the histogram `.copy-node` button and the raw payload's `#payload-json-viewer` button keep the stock in-content button paint. This plan appends the payload rules to the landed `about:telemetry` body — no new `@-moz-document` body, so the sheet's body-count assertion stays at six — reusing only values the sheet and test module already pin, so no new constant and no new hex is introduced and no landed rule changes. The home-section chrome stays Firefox's, as the landed part-1 grounding recorded.

**Verified facts (checked 2026-10-27 against the installed Firefox ESR 153.5.1's omnijar contents, scratch at `/tmp/tum-scratch-omz/omni`).** `aboutTelemetry.xhtml` builds every section inside `div#main.main-content`, each data section holding a JS-filled `div.data` (`#general-data`, `#environment-data`, `#session-info`, `#scalars`, `#keyed-scalars`, `#histograms`, `#keyed-histograms`, `#events`, `#simple-measurements`, `#slow-sql-tables`, `#addon-details`); `#raw-payload-section` holds `button#payload-json-viewer` and `pre#raw-payload-data`. `aboutTelemetry.js` builds the tables as bare `table` > `caption`/`tr`/`th`/`td` (`renderTable`, `renderAddonDetails`, `renderSlowSQL`) and each histogram as `div.histogram` (id = the probe name) wrapping `div.histogram-title`, `div.histogram-stats`, the bars and `button.copy-node`; each bar is `div.bar` (inline padding-top/height) wrapping `div.bar-inner`. `aboutTelemetry.css` paints the stock the plan must replace: `.histogram { border: 1px solid var(--border-color); background-color: var(--background-color-box); border-radius: 2px }`, `.bar-inner { background-color: var(--color-accent-primary); border: 1px solid rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-radius: 2px }`, `td { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-color) }` and `tr:not(:first-child):hover { background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) }`; `.copy-node`'s visibility/position and `.histogram:hover .copy-node { visibility: visible }` are geometry that stays stock, as do `.histogram`'s float/padding/min-height, `.bar`'s width/float/font, the caption/table font sizes and `.keyed-histogram`/`.sub-section` margins. `grep -c histogram` and `grep -c copy-node` return 0 for the sheet and the test module: nothing landed or planned covers the payloads, and the landed part-1 plan recorded exactly this scope as the later plan's subject.

**Grounding (platform adaptation, steward clarification 2026-10-25).** No reference screenshot shows Firefox's about:telemetry (the same missing surface the landed telemetry row of `docs/invariants.md` records): the tables reuse the landed about:support/about:networking table arms byte-for-byte (the sunken white table field of `FIELD_RULE`, the `#EEEEEE` zebra of `TROUGH`, the raised `#DDDDDD` `th` band of `SUPPORT_TH_RULE`, the cleared cell borders of `SUPPORT_CELL_RULE`, the flat `#CCCCFF` `th:hover` of `BUTTON_HOVER_RULE`); the `.histogram` box reuses the landed `#ping-picker` panel values byte-for-byte (the sheet's white face and square `1px solid #000000` outline, no shadow); `.bar-inner` uses a flat adaptation (2026-10-28) of the ten-row progress gradient in `widgets/bar_meter_horizontal.svg` pinned by `tests/test_desktoptheme_progressbar.py::TestProgressBar`, choosing the `#CCCCFF` selection colour pinned by `tests/test_colorscheme_reference.py::TestReferenceAnchors.test_selection_background`, with `border: 0` and `border-radius: 0`; the `.copy-node` and `#payload-json-viewer` buttons reuse the landed push-button recipe `BUTTON_RULE`/`BUTTON_HOVER_RULE` (grounded in `widgets/button.svg` and `aboutsystem_betawiki.png`, pinned by `tests/test_desktoptheme_button.py::TestButton` and `TestButtonReference`). ### Platinum GTK file chooser: paint the places sidebar band and its rows as the menu-bar face with the landed list-row selection in GTK 3 and GTK 4 (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; independent of the queued about:telemetry furniture plan — that one touches `theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userContent.css` and `tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py`, this one the GTK sheets and their suites, and their `docs/invariants.md` edits only append one new row each, so either order merges; the chooser's path bar landed in PLANS-DONE.md and its file list, column headers, entries, buttons, action bar and paned handle are already covered by the landed generic rules, so the places sidebar is the chooser's remaining surface) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** After the landed path-bar plan, a GTK file chooser's places sidebar — the left column `GtkFileChooserWidget` shows in both toolkits — still paints stock: the band keeps Adwaita's near-white `#fbfafa` face (GTK 3 with a `#f9f9f8` backdrop face; GTK 4 with a grey `#cdc7c2` right border), GTK 3 greys the rows in backdrop (`placessidebar row:backdrop { color: #929595 }` and `placessidebar row:backdrop:selected { color: #fcfcfc }`), a selected row in an inactive GTK 3 window turns Adwaita blue (`row.activatable:selected:backdrop { background-color: #3584e4 }`, outranking the landed selection rule, which has no backdrop arm), and the sidebar's "New bookmark" row keeps Adwaita's link-blue text in both toolkits. This plan paints the sidebar band as the landed flat menu-bar face — `#DDDDDD`, black text, flat backdrop, no border — and pins the chooser-specific row arms, introducing no new hex and editing no landed rule.

**Verified facts (checked 2026-10-27, PyGObject probes with GTK 3.24.49 and GTK 4.18.6 plus the stock sheets extracted from the installed libraries' gresources).** A GTK 3 `Gtk.FileChooserDialog` builds `paned.horizontal > placessidebar[frame, sidebar] > viewport.frame > list > row[activatable, sidebar-row]` rows (one carries `sidebar-new-bookmark-row`); the chooser's header strip holds the `path-bar` (landed) beside a `search` entry (landed), the file list is `treeview.view` (landed) and the bottom bar an `actionbar` (landed). A GTK 4 `Gtk.FileChooserWidget` builds `paned.horizontal > placessidebar[sidebar] > scrolledwindow > viewport > list[navigation-sidebar] > row[activatable, sidebar-row]` rows (plus one `sidebar-new-bookmark-row`); its root `filechooser` node's other paint — the `pathbar` (landed), the `columnview.view` file list (landed), the search `entry` (landed) and the root `actionbar` band (landed) — is covered by landed rules. Stock paint, from the GTK 3 gresource `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Adwaita/gtk-contained.css` and the GTK 4 gresource `/org/gtk/libgtk/theme/Default/Default-light.css`: GTK 3 paints `.sidebar { border-style: none; background-color: #fbfafa }` with `.sidebar:backdrop { background-color: #f9f9f8 }`; GTK 4 paints `.sidebar { background-color: #fbfafa }` with `.sidebar:not(separator):dir(ltr) { border-right: 1px solid #cdc7c2 }`; GTK 3 paints `placessidebar row:backdrop { color: #929595 }`, `placessidebar row:backdrop:selected { color: #fcfcfc }`, `row.activatable:selected:backdrop { background-color: #3584e4 }` and `placessidebar row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row { color: #3584e4 }`; GTK 4 paints `placessidebar .navigation-sidebar > row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row { color: #3584e4 }`. The landed generic arms already paint rest, hover (transparent) and selection (`#CCCCFF`, black text, square): `list row.activatable:hover` and `list row.activatable:selected[:hover]` outrank stock's `row.activatable:hover` and GTK 4's `.navigation-sidebar > row:hover/:selected/:selected:hover`, so only the band face, the backdrop arms, the GTK 4 right border and the new-bookmark text remain stock. The sidebar's inner `list` already stays transparent because stock's `.sidebar list { background-color: transparent }` (0,1,1) beats our landed white `list` rule (0,1,0); stock's `placessidebar > viewport.frame { border-style: none }` likewise already clears the inner viewport's frame against our landed `.frame` rule in GTK 3. `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_disabled_text_follows_the_entry_text_rule` already establishes that our theme sheet loads after the stock base and wins equal-specificity ties by order, so tie-overrides need no `!important`.

**Grounding (platform adaptation, steward clarification 2026-10-25).** No reference screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a GTK widget, and Mac OS 8.6's Finder has no sidebar at all, so the band reuses the reference-grounded flat menu-bar/window face `#DDDDDD` with black text (the landed `window, .background` face) and a flat `#DDDDDD` backdrop mirroring the landed headerbar's inactive face; the rows reuse the landed `list row` recipe whose `#CCCCFF` selection is the pinned `[Colors:Selection]` of `tests/test_colorscheme_reference.py::TestReferenceAnchors::test_selection_background` and whose squareness extends the landed `border-radius: 0` selection. The `placessidebar` node name, the `sidebar`, `frame`, `navigation-sidebar` and `sidebar-new-bookmark-row` classes, the stock row geometry (the 36px min-height, stock paddings and margins) and the drag-over indicator (`:drop(active)` arms, painted green by stock) are GTK-required; the rows' geometry and the drag indicator stay stock. Recorded, not planned here: the same GTK 3 `:backdrop` arms grey or blue every generic list row in an inactive window (our landed row rule has no backdrop arm outside the sidebar) — a natural subject of a later plan deciding whether the landed row recipe grows backdrop arms generally.

**Approach.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, append after the landed `.path-bar > button` block at the sheet's end:

```css
/* A file chooser's places sidebar takes the flat menu-bar face with black
   text in backdrop, and its rows keep the landed selection and drop
   Adwaita's link blue. */
.sidebar {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  color: #000000;
}

.sidebar:backdrop {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  color: #000000;
}

placessidebar row:backdrop {
  color: #000000;
}

placessidebar row.activatable:selected:backdrop {
  background-color: #CCCCFF;
  color: #000000;
}

placessidebar row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row {
  color: #000000;
}
```

`.sidebar` ties stock's `.sidebar` face on specificity and wins by coming later; `placessidebar row:backdrop` (0,1,2) and `placessidebar row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row` (0,1,2) tie and win the same way; `placessidebar row.activatable:selected:backdrop` (0,2,2) beats stock's `row.activatable:selected:backdrop` (0,2,1). GTK 3 keeps the landed `.frame` sunken black box around the chooser's sidebar (the `frame` class is on the `placessidebar` itself) and stock's `placessidebar > viewport.frame` clear.

In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, append at the sheet's end after the landed `pathbar` block:

```css
/* A file chooser's places sidebar takes the flat menu-bar face and drops
   the stock grey right border; its new-bookmark row drops Adwaita's link
   blue. */
.sidebar {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  color: #000000;
  border: none;
}

.sidebar:backdrop {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  color: #000000;
}

placessidebar.sidebar:not(separator):dir(ltr),
placessidebar.sidebar:not(separator):dir(rtl) {
  border: none;
}

placessidebar .navigation-sidebar > row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row {
  color: #000000;
}
```

The border-clearing rule spells the stock arms `.sidebar:not(separator):dir(ltr)`/`:dir(rtl)` through the `placessidebar.sidebar` node so it ties (0,3,0) with stock's border-right rule and wins by coming later; plain `placessidebar.sidebar { border: none }` (0,1,1) would lose to (0,3,0) and is spelled only as part of that rule. GTK 4 needs no row backdrop arms: stock's `.navigation-sidebar > row` has none, so the landed selection and transparent hover hold in backdrop too.

In `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, add `TestGtkTheme.test_places_sidebar` mirroring `test_path_bar_tabs`'s `assert_rule` idiom with the spec-module constants (`FACE`, `BLACK`, `SELECTION` from `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, which re-exports the pinned `platinum_palette.py` values):

- `assert_rule(".sidebar", {"background-color": FACE, "color": BLACK})` and `assert_rule(".sidebar:backdrop", {"background-color": FACE, "color": BLACK})`.
- `assert_rule("placessidebar row:backdrop", {"color": BLACK})`.
- `assert_rule("placessidebar row.activatable:selected:backdrop", {"background-color": SELECTION, "color": BLACK})`.
- `assert_rule("placessidebar row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row", {"color": BLACK})`.

In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, add `TestGtk4Theme.test_places_sidebar` with the same first two band assertions plus:

- `assert_rule("placessidebar.sidebar:not(separator):dir(ltr)", {"border": "none"})` and the same for the `:dir(rtl)` selector.
- `assert_rule("placessidebar .navigation-sidebar > row.sidebar-new-bookmark-row", {"color": BLACK})`.

Both suites' existing exact-set and palette tests (the sheets' `@define-color` register and hex checks in `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`/`tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`) must stay green without edits — the new rules reuse only `#DDDDDD`, `#CCCCFF` and `#000000`.

In `docs/invariants.md`, in the `## gtk` table, append one row after the current last row (the tree-header row) before the trailing validation notes: the guarantee in one sentence — both GTK sheets paint the file chooser's places sidebar band (`placessidebar`, the `sidebar` class) as the flat `#DDDDDD` menu-bar face with black text and a flat `#DDDDDD` backdrop, clear GTK 4's stock grey right border, keep GTK 3's rows black-texted in backdrop with the landed `#CCCCFF` square selection in backdrop, and paint the `sidebar-new-bookmark-row` black while the rows' geometry and drag-over indicator stay stock — with the test column naming `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_places_sidebar` and `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_places_sidebar`, and the provenance cell naming the missing reference surface (no reference screenshot shows a GTK widget; the Finder has no sidebar), the reused face (the landed `window, .background` band) and row selection (`widgets/listitem.svg`'s flat fill, `test_selection_background`), the gresource and PyGObject probes above, the GTK-required node and class names, and that declaration checks establish no rendered pixels. Trim no landed row; `tests/test_invariants.py` (part of the check) parses the register.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Both sheets carry exactly the rules spelled above; no landed rule's text changes; the only hex values introduced are the already-pinned `#DDDDDD`, `#CCCCFF` and `#000000`.
- `TestGtkTheme.test_places_sidebar` and `TestGtk4Theme.test_places_sidebar` pass against the sheets, and every landed GTK test keeps passing with no edits outside the additions.

**Files touched.** `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, `docs/invariants.md`. ### Firefox Platinum content: paint about:telemetry's page furniture — the category sidebar rows, the section-filter search field and store menu and the ping-picker panel — with the landed nav-row, line-edit, menulist and panel recipes (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; the recorded first half of the about:telemetry work — the data payloads, the sections' tables, the histogram bars, the copy buttons and the raw-JSON viewers, are the natural subjects of a later plan whose reuse of this plan's furniture recipes and this page's remaining surfaces is decided then, so no design question is left open here; independent of the queued about:networking sidebar plan — the two touch the same sheet and test module, so all anchors below are rule texts and symbol names, never line numbers) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed `userContent.css` sheet paints the about:downloads list, the about:config field, the about:preferences pane, the about:support tables and buttons and the about:networking tables and buttons; Firefox's about:telemetry page keeps its stock paint entirely. This plan paints the page's furniture: its `#categories` sidebar rows (including the dynamically added `.category-subsection` rows), the `.header` strip's `#search` filter field and `#stores` store menu, and the floating `#ping-picker` panel each take the landed recipe byte-for-byte, reusing only values the sheet and test module already pin, so no new constant and no new hex is introduced and no landed rule changes. The sections' data payloads stay stock here.

**Verified facts (checked 2026-10-27, Firefox ESR 153.5.1; probe scratch at `/tmp/tum-scratch-omz/omni`).** `chrome/toolkit/content/global/aboutTelemetry.xhtml` is the light-DOM page (no `attachShadow` in it, its `.css` or its `.js`): `div#categories` holds fourteen static `div.category.category-no-icon` rows each wrapping `span.category-name`, the first carrying `class="category category-no-icon has-data selected"` at load, and `aboutTelemetry.css`'s `.category:not(.has-data) { display: none }` hides every row until data exists, so the paint need not special-case the badge. `aboutTelemetry.js` flips the selection with the CLASS, never an attribute (unlike about:networking's `[selected]`-attribute-only rule): `current_button = document.querySelector(".category.selected"); current_button.classList.remove("selected"); selected.classList.add("selected")`, and `showSubSection` does the same with `.category-subsection.selected`; the subsection rows appear only when JS adds them (aboutTelemetry.css gives `.category.selected > .category-subsection { display: block }`), so the handles are `#categories > .category.selected` and `#categories .category-subsection.selected`. The stock row paint comes from `chrome://global/skin/classic/global/in-content/common-shared.css`, whose `#categories > .category`, `:hover`, `:hover:active`, `.category.selected` and `:focus-visible` arms are the very arms the sheet's landing about:networking body already overrides with `!important`. The `.header` strip (aboutTelemetry.css) holds `h1#sectionTitle`, `label#storesLabel`, `select#stores` (hidden until the JS displays a store list) and `input[type="text"]#search` in `div#sectionFilters`; `#search` sits outside `.main-content`, so the landing table-field arm does not reach it. `#ping-picker` is a fixed-position panel `aboutTelemetry.css` paints `--background-color-box` on `--border-color` with `border-radius: 2px` and `box-shadow: 0 1px 3px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.25)`; it is stock white-on-white in the light scheme and our square black outline replaces that shadow. @-moz-document url("about:telemetry") {
```css
  /* The category sidebar rows, the section-filter field and store menu
```

### Firefox Platinum content: paint about:networking's category sidebar rows, the DNS-lookup host field and the autorefresh checkbox as the landed nav-row, line-edit and check-box recipes (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; extends the landed about:networking plan in PLANS-DONE.md, whose header paragraph records these three surfaces as "the natural subjects of a later plan"; independent of the queued GTK path-bar plan — it touches only the Firefox sheet and its tests) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed about:networking plan painted the page's ten `.main-content` tables and four buttons and recorded that `#categories` (its eight `.category` rows), the DNS-lookup tool's `#host` text field and the autorefresh `#autorefcheck` checkbox stay Firefox's, naming them "the natural subjects of a later plan; this is decided here so no design question is left open". This is that later plan: the same `@-moz-document url("about:networking")` body gains four more rule groups — the sidebar rows as the landed about:preferences nav-row paint (flat transparent rest, flat `#CCCCFF` black-text hover/active and selected faces, square corners), `#host` as the landed Platinum line edit, and `#autorefcheck` as the landed preferences check box face with the shipped check-mark data URI — reusing only values the sheet and tests already pin, so no new constant and no new hex beyond the landed `#888888` checkbox-bevel arm is introduced, and no landed rule text changes.

**Verified facts (checked 2026-10-27, installed Firefox ESR 153.5.1).** `chrome/toolkit/content/global/aboutNetworking.html` is the light-DOM page at about:networking (the landed paragraph's established `attachShadow` count 0): `div#categories` holds eight `div.category.category-no-icon` children each wrapping `span.category-name`, the first carrying `selected="true"`; `aboutNetworking.js` (line ~358–360 of that file) flips the selection only through the `selected` attribute — `current_button.removeAttribute("selected"); button.setAttribute("selected", "true")` — never a class, so the row handle is `#categories > .category[selected]`. The stock row paint comes from `chrome/toolkit/skin/classic/global/in-content/common-shared.css`: `#categories > .category` is a button-like row (`border: var(--button-border)`, `border-radius: var(--border-radius-small)`, `transition: background-color 150ms`), `:hover` and `:hover:active` paint `--button-background-color-hover`/`-active` faces with hover accent colours, and `#categories > .category[selected], #categories > .category.selected` recolour the text to `--color-accent-primary` while `[selected]:not(:hover)` clears the background — a keyboard `:focus-visible` outline stays stock. `#dnslookuptool` holds `input[type="text"]#host` between its label and `#dnsLookupButton` (already painted), and `#refreshDiv` holds `input#autorefcheck[type="checkbox"]` with its l10n `span` beside it; `common-shared.css`'s `html|input:where([type="checkbox"], [type="radio"])` block sizes both native inputs `height/width: var(--checkbox-size)`, so the box keeps that stock size under `appearance: none` and no metric is added. The landed sheet body the plan extends is the file's last `@-moz-document url("about:networking")` block; `tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py` presses it through `SheetCase` (`self.rules`, `self.selectors`, `self.bodies`), the module register `REQUIRED_NETWORKING_RULES`/`NETWORKING_SELECTORS`, and `FORBIDDEN_PAGE_CHROME = ("body", "h1", "hgroup", "main-content-title")`. `tests/support/selector_matching.py`'s matcher (docstring, `matches`) supports tag/id/class/attribute selectors and `:hover` only — no `:checked` — so the `:checked` and `:hover:active` arms stay pinned by selector text and the exact-register test exactly as the landed `:nth-child(2n)` zebra arm already is.

**Grounding (platform adaptation, steward clarification 2026-10-25).** No reference screenshot shows Firefox's about:networking (established by the landed paragraph) — these rules sample no reference pixel: the sidebar rows reuse the landed about:preferences nav-row values (transparent rest, flat `#CCCCFF` hover/active/selected, black text, radius 0) whose `#CCCCFF` is the pinned `[Colors:Selection]` of `tests/test_colorscheme_reference.py::TestReferenceAnchors.test_selection_background` and whose squareness extends the landed list-row `border-radius: 0` of the sheet's own downloads/list recipes; `#host` reuses the landed line-edit field byte-recipe (`#FFFFFF` face, black text, square `1px solid #000000`, `inset 1px 1px #999999` — `FIELD_RULE` in the test register, grounded in `widgets/lineedit.svg` and pinned by `tests/test_desktoptheme_lineedit.py::TestLineEdit` and `TestLineEditReference`); `#autorefcheck` reuses the landed about:preferences check-box face (`#DDDDDD` face, square `1px solid #000000`, `inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #888888`, whose raised bevel owns the Kvantum check-box provenance) and its checked arm's shipped check-mark data URI, pinned by `tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py`'s `CHECKBOX_FACE_RULE`/`CHECKBOX_GLYPH_RULE`. The `#categories`, `.category`, `[selected]`, `input#autorefcheck`, `input[type="text"]#host`, `:hover`/`:hover:active`/`:checked` arms and the stock `--checkbox-size` sizing are Firefox-required; the sidebar keeps Firefox's non-selected-row stock hover cleared only where our paint lands, and the `:focus-visible` outline stays Firefox's.

```css

  #categories > .category {
```

### Platinum GTK path bar: paint the file chooser's breadcrumb buttons as the Platinum tabs in GTK 3 and GTK 4 (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; independent of the stack-switcher plan, which landed while this entry waited — it touches the same three landed files, so all anchors below are rule texts and symbol names, not line numbers) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed GTK sheets give the generic `button` the raised Platinum push-button paint and `button:active, button:checked` a sunken bevel, and a file chooser's path bar — the breadcrumb strip `GtkFileChooserWidget` shows above the file list — falls through to exactly those rules: every unpressed breadcrumb gets the generic raised face, and the current folder's `GtkToggleButton` sits `:checked` for the chooser's whole lifetime, so the breadcrumb strip paints its home entry *permanently sunken* while a queued stack window's own header strip would paint the same strip's active entry as the raised, flat-merged `tab:checked` face. This plan paints the path bar's buttons with the landed tab recipe byte-for-byte in both toolkits — the same decision the landed stack-switcher plan made for that widget — so the unpressed breadcrumbs read as raised tabs, the current folder as the flat checked tab, and no new constant, no new hex and no edit to any landed rule is introduced.

**Verified facts (checked 2026-10-27).** `grep -c "pathbar\|path-bar"` returns 0 for `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, `tests/support/gtk_rule_cases.py` and `docs/invariants.md`, and no `## Planned` entry nor PLANS-DONE.md or BUGS-FIXED.md finished record names a GTK path bar. Live-probed with PyGObject (GTK 3.24.49 and GTK 4.18.6, the toolkits the landed status-bar row names), a `Gtk.FileChooserWidget` opened on `/usr/local/share` builds: GTK 3 — a `GtkPathBar` having `get_style_context().list_classes() == ["linked", "path-bar"]` whose direct `get_children()` are the folder `GtkToggleButton`s with classes `text-button, toggle` (`image-button, toggle` for the leading icon button), two `GtkButton`s with class `slider-button` (the scroll arrows) and one `GtkMenuButton` with classes `popup, toggle` (the "Other Locations" button the chooser root shows); GTK 4 — a root `get_css_name() == "pathbar"` widget whose only `button` descendants sit at `pathbar > scrolledwindow > viewport > box[linked,horizontal] > button` (the folder toggles with classes `text-button, toggle` / `image-button, toggle`), the scrolledwindow's overlay `scrollbar` siblings carrying no `button` node. In GTK 3 the `GtkPathBar` widget-path's own node name resolves `None`, so the widget-set `path-bar` and `linked` classes are the reachable handle; in GTK 4 the root's `pathbar` css node is the handle and no `path-bar` class exists. The current folder's toggle carries `:checked` in both toolkits. The landed rules these selectors must outrank in both sheets are `button { ... box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA; }` and `button:active, button:checked { box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #AAAAAA, inset -1px -1px #FFFFFF; }` — the checked arm is what paints the sunken face this plan clears. The landed tab recipe the sheets already ship is the `tab`/`tab.reorderable-page` arm block (`tab`, `tab:hover`, `tab:checked`, `tab:checked:hover` plus the same `tab:backdrop[:checked]` arms, each rule also naming the `notebook > header > tabs > tab[:...][:...]` spellings), and the suite shares it through `TAB_STATES` in `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py` (states `base`, `hover`, `checked`, `checked+hover`, `backdrop`, `backdrop+checked`) with `RAISED_BEVEL` (`inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #999999`), while `GtkSheetRuleCases.test_tab_states` in `tests/support/gtk_rule_cases.py` builds each state's expected dict from `FACE`, `BLACK` and `RAISED_BEVEL` via the landed `assert_rule`; the landed tests that drive `test_tab_states` live in the suites' `TestGtkTheme`/`TestGtk4Theme` inheritance of that shared class.

**Grounding (platform adaptation, steward clarification 2026-10-25).** No reference screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a GTK path bar, and Mac OS 8.6 has no breadcrumb surface at all — a Finder window navigates through a pop-up folder menu, not a button strip — so the plan samples no new reference pixel: it reuses only the landed tab recipe's values, whose own provenance the landed `test_tab_states` path already records (the raised tab bevel and the `#DDDDDD` face, pinned by the desktop theme's `widgets/tabbar.svg` case and the notebook tab rules). The `path-bar`/`linked` classes, the `pathbar`, `scrolledwindow`, `viewport` and `box` node names and the checked folder button's `:checked` state are GTK-required (probe above). The kept `border-bottom-color: #DDDDDD` on the checked arm — meaningful where a notebook tab merges into its header groove — is included byte-for-byte against this plan's decided reopening: below a path bar sits the chooser's black-outlined sunken file field, so the checked folder's bottom border paints `#DDDDDD` over one pixel of that outline; this is recorded here as the decided adaptation so no design question is left open. `:backdrop` stays out of scope, as the landed infobar, search-bar, action-bar and status-bar decisions and the queued stack-switcher plan scoped it out, and the landed tab `:backdrop` arms stay untouched.

**Approach.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, directly after the landed `statusbar > frame > border` rule (the sheet's last rule), add

```css
/* A file chooser's path bar draws its breadcrumb buttons — the folder toggles,
   the slider arrows and the Other Locations button alike — as the landed tab
   recipe, the current folder's checked tab included; :backdrop stays out of
   scope. */
.path-bar > button {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  background-image: none;
  border: 1px solid #000000;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #999999;
}

.path-bar > button:hover {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  background-image: none;
  border: 1px solid #000000;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #999999;
}

.path-bar > button:checked,
.path-bar > button:checked:hover {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  background-image: none;
  border: 1px solid #000000;
  border-bottom-color: #DDDDDD;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: none;
}
```

Verification that the three blocks' declaration lines match the landed tab arms' text byte-for-byte is part of the edit; so is laying the comment out before the first arm and nothing between the arms.

In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, directly after the landed final `statusbar` rule (the sheet's last rule), add the same three blocks under the same comment text with `pathbar > scrolledwindow > viewport > box > button`, `pathbar > scrolledwindow > viewport > box > button:hover` and `pathbar > scrolledwindow > viewport > box > button:checked, pathbar > scrolledwindow > viewport > box > button:checked:hover` as the selectors.

In both sheets' provenance header comments, append one sentence immediately before the closing `*/`: "A file chooser's path bar paints its buttons as the landed tab recipe byte-for-byte; no reference screenshot shows a GTK path bar, and the path-bar and linked classes and the pathbar, scrolledwindow, viewport and box node names are GTK-required."

In `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme`, after the landed `test_status_bar_frame_border_is_flat`, add `test_path_bar_tabs`: build the local dict `forms = {"base": ".path-bar > button", "hover": ".path-bar > button:hover", "checked": ".path-bar > button:checked", "checked+hover": ".path-bar > button:checked:hover"}` and iterate `TAB_STATES`, skipping every state whose name is not in the dict (the two `:backdrop` states stay out of scope), building for the state iterated the same expected dict `test_tab_states` builds — `FACE` face, `background-image: none`, `border: 1px solid BLACK`, `border-radius: 0`, and `box-shadow: RAISED_BEVEL` when unchecked, `border-bottom-color: FACE` and `box-shadow: none` when checked — and calling `self.assert_rule(selector, expected)` inside a `subTest(state=..., selector=...)` per selector, with no change to `test_status_bar`, `test_status_bar_frame_border_is_flat` or the shared `GtkSheetRuleCases`.

In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme`, after the landed `test_status_bar`, add the same `test_path_bar_tabs` body with the four `pathbar > scrolledwindow > viewport > box > button` selector spellings. Each suite's existing `from support.gtk_theme_spec import (...)` list gains `TAB_STATES` only if it is not already there (the landed stack-switcher plan added it to both suites, so no import change is needed).

Extend no landed assertion: the shared `assert_rule` machinery already parses both sheets, `test_tab_states` changes no text and runs unchanged, and the only shared-file touch is the one added `TAB_STATES` name per suite's already existing import list.

In `docs/invariants.md`, in the `## gtk` table: append exactly one row after the landed status-bar row (the table's current last row before the trailing validation notes) with the guarantee in one sentence (both sheets paint a file chooser's path bar as the landed tab recipe — the raised bevel for the unpressed states and the flat checked face with the face-coloured bottom border — while the landed notebook tab and generic button rules stay byte-identical and an unfocused chooser keeps them) and the test column naming `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_path_bar_tabs` and `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_path_bar_tabs`; its exception sentence names the missing reference surface (no reference screenshot shows a GTK path bar, and Mac OS 8.6 has no breadcrumb to adapt), the re-used landed values through `test_tab_states`, and the probed GTK 3 class / GTK 4 node handles. Trim no landed row; `tests/support/invariants.py`'s register stays in step.

**Files touched.** `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Implementation note (2026-10-27 by the feature role).** The stack-switcher plan landed while this entry sat in `## Planned`, so two anchors moved with it: both suites' import lists already carried `TAB_STATES` (no import change was needed, as the plan itself allowed for), and the invariants row landed after the stack-switcher row — the table's current last row before the trailing validation notes — rather than directly after the status-bar row. Both sheets' rule anchors (the GTK 3 `statusbar > frame > border` rule and the GTK 4 final `statusbar` rule) were still the sheets' last rules and matched as written.

### Platinum GTK stack switcher: paint its page buttons as the Platinum tabs in GTK 3 and GTK 4 (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; the `## Planned` queue holds the status-bar plan ahead of it, which touches the same three landed files, so both anchors below are rule texts and symbol names, not line numbers) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed GTK sheets paint a `GtkSwitcher`'s pages (the landed `notebook` tab rules) as the Platinum raised tabs and paint generic push buttons with the raised bevel, but a `GtkStackSwitcher` — the page-group buttons file choosers and stack windows place at a window's top — falls through to the landed generic button rules, so its active page button paints as the landed `button:checked` *sunken* face instead of a raised tab, disagreeing with the landed notebook tab beside which stack switchers appear. This plan paints the stack switcher's child buttons with the landed tab recipe byte-for-byte in both toolkits, so the active page reads as the raised, flat-merged tab and the inactive pages as unpressed tabs, with no new constant, no new hex and no edit to any landed rule.

**Verified facts (checked 2026-10-27).** `grep -c stackswitcher` returns 0 for `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py`, `tests/support/gtk_rule_cases.py` and `docs/invariants.md`, and no PLANS.md `## Planned` entry nor PLANS-DONE.md or BUGS-FIXED.md finished record names a GTK stack switcher. Live-probed with PyGObject (GTK 3.24.49 and GTK 4.18.6, the toolkits the landed infobar row names): a `Gtk.StackSwitcher` with two pages builds a GTK 3 tree `Window > stackswitcher[stack-switcher,linked,horizontal] > button[text-button,radio]` (the children are `Gtk.RadioButton`s with `relief` 0; the node carries the `radio` *class*, not the `radio` node, so the landed `radio:checked` glyph rule cannot match it) and a GTK 4 tree root css name `stackswitcher` with class `linked` over `button` children with classes `text-button, toggle` (probe of `get_css_name()`/`get_css_classes()`). docs.gtk.org states on both the GtkStackSwitcher pages that the widget has a single CSS node named `stackswitcher`, so the root `stackswitcher` node is the guaranteed handle in both toolkits, and the active page's button carries `:checked` in each (a toggle-type button the stack switches active). The landed generic rules both sheets carry — `button { ... box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA; }` and `button:active, button:checked { box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #AAAAAA, inset -1px -1px #FFFFFF; }` — by themselves paint the checked page button *sunken*, the only repaint this plan must clear. The landed tab recipe the sheets already ship (`tab`, `tab:hover`, `tab:checked`, `tab:checked:hover` and the same `tab:backdrop[:checked]` arms) and the suite shares it through `TAB_STATES` in `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py` with `RAISED_BEVEL` (=`inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #999999`, the tab bevel differing from the `button` bevel's `#AAAAAA` depth), `test_tab_states` in `tests/support/gtk_rule_cases.py::GtkSheetRuleCases` builds each state's expected declaration list from `FACE` and `BLACK`; both GTK suites already import `RAISED_BEVEL`, `FACE`, and `BLACK`, and neither imports `TAB_STATES` yet.

**Grounding (platform adaptation, steward clarification 2026-10-25).** No reference screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a GTK stack switcher, so the plan samples no new reference pixel: it reuses only the landed tab recipe's values, whose own provenance the landed `test_tab_states` path already records (the raised tab bevel and the `#DDDDDD` face, pinned by the desktop theme's `widgets/tabbar.svg` case and the notebook tab rules). The `stackswitcher` root node and the `button` child nodes are GTK-required; so is the checked page button's `:checked` state. The checked arm reuses the tab checked recipe byte-for-byte — including the tab's face-coloured `border-bottom-color`, meaningful only where a notebook tab merges with its header — so the sheets keep exactly one tab recipe; this is decided here so no design question is left open. `:backdrop` stays out of scope, as the landed infobar, search-bar and action-bar decisions scoped it out, and the landed tab `:backdrop` arms stay untouched, so an unfocused stack window keeps the landed generic button paint unless a stackswitcher-specific rule matches.

**Approach.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, directly after the landed `tab:checked:hover, ... notebook > header > tabs > tab:checked:hover` rule and before the landed `treeview.view header button` rule, add

```css
/* A stack switcher's page buttons draw as the landed tab recipe, the active
   page's button included; :backdrop stays out of scope. */
stackswitcher > button {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  background-image: none;
  border: 1px solid #000000;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #999999;
}

stackswitcher > button:hover {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  background-image: none;
  border: 1px solid #000000;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #999999;
}

stackswitcher > button:checked,
stackswitcher > button:checked:hover {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  background-image: none;
  border: 1px solid #000000;
  border-bottom-color: #DDDDDD;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: none;
}
```

Verification of the selectors' spellings against the landed tab arms above them is part of the edit: the three blocks reuse the landed arm declaration lines byte-for-byte apart from the importing selector.

In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, directly after the landed `tab:backdrop:checked, ... notebook > header > tabs > tab.reorderable-page:backdrop:checked` rule and before the landed `columnview.view > header > button, treeview.view > header > button` rule, add the same block under the same comment text.

In both sheets' provenance header comments, append one sentence after the search-bar/action-bar sentence and before the closing `*/`: "A stack switcher's page buttons paint as the landed tab recipe byte-for-byte; no reference screenshot shows a GTK stack switcher, and the stackswitcher and button node names are GTK-required."

In `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme`, after the landed `test_action_bar`, add `test_stack_switcher_tabs`: build a local dict `forms = {"base": ("stackswitcher > button",), "hover": ("stackswitcher > button:hover",), "checked": ("stackswitcher > button:checked",), "checked+hover": ("stackswitcher > button:checked:hover",)}`, and iterate `TAB_STATES` skipping every state whose name is not in the dict (the two `:backdrop` states stay out of scope), building the same expected declaration list for the state iterated as `test_tab_states` does — `FACE` face, `background-image: none`, `border: 1px solid BLACK`, `border-radius: 0`, and `box-shadow: RAISED_BEVEL` when unchecked, `border-bottom-color: FACE` and `box-shadow: none` when checked — calling `self.assert_rule(selector, expected)` inside a `subTest(state=..., selector=...)` per selector, with no change to `test_tab_states` or the shared cases file.

### Platinum GTK status bar: paint `GtkStatusbar` as the menu-bar band in GTK 3 and GTK 4 (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; the `## Planned` queue holds no other entry, so nothing waits beside or behind this plan, which touches `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` and appends exactly one row to `docs/invariants.md`; no other GTK plan waits behind it) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed GTK sheets paint the menu bar, toolbar, infobar, search bar and action bar as the Platinum band (`#DDDDDD` face, black text, `#888888`/`#FFFFFF` etched bottom rule) but a `GtkStatusbar` — the long-lived bottom strip that GTK 4 still ships to GTK 3-era status-window applications — keeps stock paint: no background of its own under the sheet's `window` colours and no etched rule, so a window's bottom status strip reads as an unbounded area. This plan paints the status bar as the landed menu-bar band, the same recipe byte-for-byte, in both toolkits, and clears one accidental paint the landed `frame > border` rule draws inside it on GTK 3.

**Verified facts (checked 2026-10-27).** `grep -c statusbar` returns 0 for `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py` and `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, and no PLANS.md `## Planned` entry nor PLANS-DONE.md or BUGS-FIXED.md finished record names a GTK status bar. Live-probed with PyGObject (GTK 3.24.49 and GTK 4.18.6, the toolkits the landed infobar row names): `Gtk.Statusbar.new()` builds a GTK 3 tree `Statusbar > Frame > Box > Label` (the `Frame`'s shadow type reads `GTK_SHADOW_NONE`) and a GTK 4 tree `statusbar > box > label` (no frame node; `Gtk.Statusbar.new()` in 4.18.6 emits a `DeprecationWarning` but the class still ships and instantiates, and libadwaita applications draw no `GtkStatusbar` at all). docs.gtk.org states on both the GtkStatusbar pages: "GtkStatusbar has a single CSS node with name `statusbar`" — so the root `statusbar` node is the one guaranteed handle in both toolkits. GTK 4.18.6's built-in css (embedded in `libgtk-4.so`) only sets `statusbar { padding: 6px 10px 6px 10px; }` — no face or border of its own, so the band's background and the etched rule are the only strip paint and the GTK-required padding stays untouched. GTK 3 consequence verified against the 3.24.49 source (`gtk/gtkframe.c`, fetched from the 3.24.49 tag): a `GtkFrame` always owns the documented `frame > border` subnode and `GTK_SHADOW_NONE` only toggles the `.flat` class on it — the landed `frame > border, .frame` rule matches `frame > border.flat` and paints its sunken field border unconditionally, so today's GTK 3 statusbar carries a sunken `#000000` box inside itself that no test pins; this plan clears that border with a scoped arm rather than leaving the band to sit around a sunken field.

**Grounding (platform adaptation, steward clarification 2026-10-25).** No reference screenshot in `macos8.6-screenshots/` shows a GTK status bar, so the strip samples no new reference pixel: it reuses only reference-grounded values the sheets already pin — the `#DDDDDD` face and black text via the menu-bar band (`tests/test_colorscheme_reference.py::TestReferenceAnchors::test_menu_bar_face`) and the etched pair (`tests/test_desktoptheme_line.py::TestLineReference`), through the sheets' landed `toolbar, menubar` and infobar rules and the shared `INFOBAR` spec. The band geometry and the `statusbar` node name are GTK-required, as is the GTK 3 `statusbar > frame > border` clearing arm's `frame`/`border` node pair. `:backdrop` stays out of scope, as the landed infobar, search-bar and action-bar decisions scoped it out, and the etched rule stays the menu-bar band's bottom rule rather than a mirrored top rule because the landed search/action bar plan decided the sheets ship exactly one band recipe and the bottom-standing action bar already took that bottom rule; this is decided here so no design question is left open.

**Approach.** In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, directly after the landed `searchbar > revealer > box, actionbar > revealer > box` rule (the GTK 3 sheet's last rule), add:

```css
/* A status bar draws the menu-bar band: the #DDDDDD face, black text and the
   etched bottom rule. The statusbar's internal shadowless GtkFrame border
   stays flat, so the landed frame rule does not draw the sunken field
   inside the band; :backdrop stays out of scope. */
statusbar {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  color: #000000;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #888888;
  box-shadow: inset 0 -1px #FFFFFF;
}

statusbar > frame > border {
  border-style: none;
  box-shadow: none;
}
```

In `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, directly after the landed `searchbar > revealer > box, actionbar > revealer > box` rule (the GTK 4 sheet's last rule), add the same band rule under a comment that drops the GtkFrame sentence and records that the GTK 4 statusbar builds `statusbar > box > label` with no frame node (verified above), so the sheet gains no clearing arm.

In both sheets' provenance header comments, append one sentence after the search-bar/action-bar sentence and before the closing `*/`: "A status bar band reuses the same menu-bar band with the same etched bottom rule, and on GTK 3 its shadowless internal frame border stays flat; no reference screenshot shows a GTK status bar, and the statusbar node name is GTK-required."

In `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme`, after the landed `test_action_bar`, add `test_status_bar` calling `self.assert_infobar(("statusbar",))` — reusing the shared `INFOBAR` spec in `tests/support/gtk_theme_spec.py` and `tests/support/gtk_rule_cases.py` so the band stays byte-identical to the landed band rules, with no new constant and no edit to any landed rule — and `test_status_bar_frame_border_is_flat` calling `self.assert_rule("statusbar > frame > border", {"border-style": "none", "box-shadow": "none"})`.

In `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme`, after the landed `test_action_bar`, add the same `test_status_bar` with the same `assert_infobar` call.

Extend no landed assertion: the shared `assert_rule` machinery already parses both sheets, so the only change is two tests in the GTK 3 suite and one in the GTK 4 suite.

In `docs/invariants.md`, in the `## gtk` table: append exactly one row after the last gtk row with the guarantee in one sentence (both sheets paint the `statusbar` node as the menu-bar band — the `#DDDDDD` face, black text and the `#888888`/`#FFFFFF` etched bottom rule — while the GTK 3 sheet keeps the statusbar's shadowless internal `frame > border` flat and the GTK 4 sheet leaves the built-in `6px 10px` statusbar padding untouched) and the test column naming `tests/test_gtk_theme.py::TestGtkTheme::test_status_bar`, `test_status_bar_frame_border_is_flat` and `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py::TestGtk4Theme::test_status_bar`; trim no landed row (this plan closes no other surface).

**Files touched.** `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The GTK 3 sheet gains exactly the two rule blocks above and the GTK 4 sheet exactly the one band rule directly after each sheet's landed search-bar/action-bar rule, introducing no hex outside `{#DDDDDD, #888888, #FFFFFF, #000000}`, changing no landed rule's text and adding no `!important`.
- Both sheets' headers gain exactly one appended sentence after the search-bar/action-bar sentence and before `*/`.
- The three new tests pass through the shared `assert_infobar`/`assert_rule` path against the landed `INFOBAR` spec, and no landed test or support constant changes.
- `docs/invariants.md` gains exactly one appended row after the last `## gtk` row naming the three new tests, with no landed row's wording changed; `tests/support/invariants.py`'s register stays in step.
- `make check` passes.

### Platinum GTK search bar and action bar: paint `GtkSearchBar` and `GtkActionBar` as the menu-bar band in GTK 3 and GTK 4 (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; independent of the waiting Firefox about:support content plan — the two touch disjoint files (`theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-3.0/gtk.css`, `theme/gtk/org.macos8.desktop/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`, `tests/test_gtk_theme.py`, `tests/test_gtk4_theme.py` versus `theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userContent.css` and `tests/test_firefox_content_theme.py`), and their `docs/invariants.md` edits only append one new row each, so either order merges; no other GTK plan waits behind it) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed GTK sheets paint the menu bar, toolbar and infobar as the Platinum band (`#DDDDDD` face, black text, `#888888`/`#FFFFFF` etched bottom rule) but a `GtkSearchBar` and a `GtkActionBar` keep stock paint: a plain background under the sheet's `window` colours with no etched rule, so a window's bottom action bar and top search bar read as unbounded strips. This plan paints both bands as the landed menu-bar band — the same recipe byte-for-byte, in both toolkits.

Live-measured with PyGObject (GTK 3.24.49 and GTK 4.18.6, the toolkits the landed infobar row also names): GTK 3 builds `searchbar > revealer > box` (the search entry under it has the `entry` node with the `.search` class) and `actionbar > revealer > box` (the buttons under it are plain `button` nodes); GTK 4's widget probes report the identical css names `searchbar > revealer > box` (a `box`-named `GtkCenterBox` under the revealer) and `actionbar > revealer > box` — so the two landed toolkits share the one selector pair, exactly as the landed infobar rule shares `infobar > revealer > box`.

Both surfaces take the one band recipe — the action bar's etched rule stays the menu-bar band's bottom rule rather than a mirrored top rule, because the sheets ship exactly one band recipe (menu bar, toolbar and infobar all use it) and a second mirrored variant would add an unpinned orientation choice; this is decided here so no design question is left open.

```css
searchbar > revealer > box,
actionbar > revealer > box {
  background-color: #DDDDDD;
  color: #000000;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #888888;
  box-shadow: inset 0 -1px #FFFFFF;
```

### Firefox Platinum chrome: Library window series, part 6/6: paint the details pane's bookmark fields, folder dropdown and tag selector as the Platinum line edits, push-button menulist and sunken list field (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; "requires part 5/6 landed" — this part appends after and edits the tail of part 5's downloads-view paint, and it narrows the stock stay-Firefox sentences that parts 1, 2 and 4 land and part 5 keeps; this is the series' last part and nothing waits behind it) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** After the landed parts, the Library window's details pane is still Firefox's: the bookmark fields, the folder dropdown and the tag selector read as the platform skin, not Platinum. In `chrome/browser/content/browser/places/places.xhtml` (read 2026-10-27 from the installed Firefox ESR 153.5.1's `browser/omni.ja`), `vbox#detailsPane` holds `vbox#itemsCountBox` and `vbox#infoBox`, and `#infoBox` embeds the bookmark editor's `#editBookmarkPanelContent` markup: labels, `html:input#editBMPanel_namePicker`, `html:input#editBMPanel_locationField`, an `hbox.editBMPanel_folderRow` holding `menulist#editBMPanel_folderMenuList.folder-icon` and `button#editBMPanel_foldersExpander.expander-down.panel-button`, `vbox#editBMPanel_folderTreeRow` holding `button#editBMPanel_newFolderButton`, `html:input#editBMPanel_tagsField` (an autocomplete input with `#editBMPanel_tagsAutocomplete` and `button#editBMPanel_tagsSelectorExpander`), `div#editBMPanel_tagsSelectorRow` holding `richlistbox#editBMPanel_tagsSelector`, and `html:input#editBMPanel_keywordField`. Paint the four fields as this sheet's Platinum line edit, the folder menulist as its Platinum push-button menulist and the tags selector as its Platinum sunken list field — the byte-recipes the landed `#editBookmarkPanel` field and menulist rules and the landed `#placesList`/`#contentAreaDownloadsView #downloadsListBox:not(:empty)` list-field rules carry (platform colour adaptations), with square rows and a flat `#CCCCFF` selected row in the tag selector and no hover rule anywhere (the landed field and list recipes have none). **Approach.** In `theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userChrome.css`, after part 5's landed `toolbar#placesToolbar toolbarbutton#clearDownloadsButton:not([disabled]):hover` rule (then the sheet's last rules), with a short comment naming the adaptations and the `#detailsPane`-only scoping reason, append six rules and nothing else:

    /* The Library details pane's bookmark fields, folder dropdown and tag
       selector adapt the sheet's landed line-edit, push-button and sunken
       list-field recipes. The same editBMPanel ids live in browser.xhtml's
       #editBookmarkPanel, whose landed rules paint its copies, and a
       detailsPane element exists only in places.xhtml, so these rules scope
       through #detailsPane. The expander buttons, the New Folder button,
       the folder tree, the labels and the popup lists stay Firefox's, as
       the landed bookmark editor's section does. */
    #detailsPane #editBMPanel_namePicker,
    #detailsPane #editBMPanel_locationField,
    #detailsPane #editBMPanel_tagsField,
    #detailsPane #editBMPanel_keywordField {
      background-color: #FFFFFF !important;
      color: #000000 !important;
      border: 1px solid #000000 !important;
      border-radius: 0 !important;
      box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999 !important;
    }

    #detailsPane #editBMPanel_folderMenuList {
      background-color: #DDDDDD !important;
      color: #000000 !important;
      border: 1px solid #000000 !important;
      border-radius: 0 !important;
      box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA !important;
    }

    #detailsPane #editBMPanel_folderMenuList:hover:not([disabled]) {
      background-color: #CCCCFF !important;
      color: #000000 !important;
      box-shadow: none !important;
    }

    #detailsPane richlistbox#editBMPanel_tagsSelector {
      appearance: none !important;
      background-color: #FFFFFF !important;
      color: #000000 !important;
      border: 1px solid #000000 !important;
      border-radius: 0 !important;
      box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999 !important;
    }

    #detailsPane richlistbox#editBMPanel_tagsSelector > richlistitem {
      border-radius: 0 !important;
    }

    #detailsPane richlistbox#editBMPanel_tagsSelector > richlistitem[selected] {
      background-color: #CCCCFF !important;
      color: #000000 !important;
    }

**Goal.** After the landed parts, the Library window's Downloads view is still Firefox's: the list field, its rows and the toolbar's Clear Downloads button read as the platform skin, not Platinum. In `chrome/browser/content/browser/places/places.xhtml` (read 2026-10-27 from the installed Firefox ESR 153.5.1's `browser/omni.ja`), `vbox#placesViewsBox` holds `tree#placeContent`'s sibling `richlistbox#downloadsListBox` (`class="allDownloadsListBox"`, `seltype="multiple"`, starting `hidden="true"`, row context `#downloadsContextMenu`), and `toolbar#placesToolbar` holds `toolbarbutton#clearDownloadsButton.tabbable` bound to `downloadsCmd_clearDownloads` beside `#libraryToolbarSpacer`. The id `#downloadsListBox` is not Library-unique: `browser.xhtml`'s `#downloadsPanel` carries the same id and its landed userChrome rules scoped through `#downloadsPanel`, and `contentAreaDownloadsView.xhtml`'s copy is painted by the landed `about:downloads` userContent rules under `@-moz-document url("about:downloads")` — so the Library rules must scope through Library-only ancestors (`#placesViewsBox`, `toolbar#placesToolbar`). `chrome/toolkit/skin/classic/global/richlistbox.css` paints `richlistbox` with `appearance: auto`/`-moz-default-appearance: listbox`, `background-color: Field`, `color: FieldText`, `border: 1px solid ThreeDShadow` and `margin: 2px 4px`, and paints `richlistitem[selected="true"]` `-moz-cellhighlight`/`-moz-cellhighlighttext` (or `SelectedItem`/`SelectedItemText` when the box is focused) and a multiple-selection focus `outline: var(--default-focusring)` in `SelectedItem`; `chrome/browser/skin/classic/browser/downloads/allDownloadsView.css` (imported by `places.xhtml`) sets `#downloadsListBox > richlistitem { min-height: 4.5em }` and, with `allDownloadsView.inc.css`, paints `--downloads-item-*` geometry and the per-row `.downloadButton` action buttons, and paints no row hover background. Paint the list as the sheet's Platinum sunken list field — `appearance: none`, `#FFFFFF` face, black text, square `1px solid #000000` outline and the `inset 1px #999999` top-left shadow, the byte-recipe the landed `#placesList`/`#placeContent` trees and the landed `#contentAreaDownloadsView #downloadsListBox:not(:empty)` userContent rule for the same widget class carry — with square rows, a flat `#CCCCFF` selected row in black text, no hover rule (the browser skin paints none and Chrome OS 8 lists have no hover: `widgets/listitem.svg` ships no hover state), and the toolbar's Clear Downloads button as the landed userChrome push button — `#DDDDDD` face, black text, square `1px solid #000000` outline and the ``inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA`` raised bevel, flat `#CCCCFF` on hover, disabled paint left to Firefox. The rows' own geometry and contents keep Firefox's: the 4.5em min-height, the `.downloadTypeIcon` 32px type icon, the `.downloadTarget`/`.downloadDetails` text layout and progress meters, the per-row `.downloadButton` action buttons (the landed about:downloads userContent rule chose the same for the twin rich list), the `richlistbox` `margin: 2px 4px` and the `--default-focusring` current-item outline.

**Approach.** In `theme/firefox/org.macos8.desktop/chrome/userChrome.css`, after the landed `menubar#placesMenu > menu[open]` title rule (part 4's appended tail, currently the sheet's last rules), with short comments naming the adaptations, append five rules and nothing else:

    /* The Library window's downloads list adapts the sheet's sunken
       list-field and row recipes (see the header's provenance
       paragraph); the browser skin paints no row hover, so there is
       no hover rule. */
    #placesViewsBox richlistbox#downloadsListBox {
      appearance: none !important;
      background-color: #FFFFFF !important;
      color: #000000 !important;
      border: 1px solid #000000 !important;
      border-radius: 0 !important;
      box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #999999 !important;
    }

    #placesViewsBox richlistbox#downloadsListBox > richlistitem {
      border-radius: 0 !important;
    }

    #placesViewsBox richlistbox#downloadsListBox > richlistitem[selected] {
      background-color: #CCCCFF !important;
      color: #000000 !important;
    }

    /* The Library's Clear Downloads button adapts the sheet's push
       button; disabled ones keep Firefox's paint. */
    toolbar#placesToolbar toolbarbutton#clearDownloadsButton:not([disabled]) {
      background-color: #DDDDDD !important;
      color: #000000 !important;
      border: 1px solid #000000 !important;
      border-radius: 0 !important;
      box-shadow: inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -1px -1px #AAAAAA !important;
    }

    toolbar#placesToolbar toolbarbutton#clearDownloadsButton:not([disabled]):hover {
      background-color: #CCCCFF !important;
      color: #000000 !important;
      box-shadow: none !important;
    }

    #mainPrefPane input[type="text"]:not([disabled]) {
